instructions: Rinse the 1 1/2 cups jasmine rice in a pot, swishing it with your fingers and pouring off the water two or three times, until the water is only a little cloudy. Add 2 1/4 cups water and bring it to a boil over high heat. Cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave the lid on for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, put the 3 tbsp sesame seeds in a large dry skillet over medium. Stir them often for 3 to 4 minutes, until they're light golden and smell toasty. Transfer them into a small bowl.

Pat the 1.5 lb chicken dry and cut it into 1 inch pieces. In a large bowl, beat the egg with 3 tbsp of the soy sauce and 1/4 cup of the cornstarch. Add the chicken and stir until it's all coated. Put the bowl in the fridge for 15 minutes.

While it chills, mince the 2 garlic cloves and grate 1 1/2 tsp of the ginger. In a medium bowl, whisk the 1 cup broth, 1/3 cup brown sugar, the remaining 1/4 cup soy sauce, the remaining 3 tbsp cornstarch, the 1 tbsp sesame oil, the ginger and the garlic. Thinly slice 3 of the scallions.

Heat 1 tbsp of the vegetable oil in the skillet over medium high until it shimmers. Add half the chicken in a single layer and leave it for 2 minutes, until the underside is golden and lets go of the pan.
Stir and cook for 3 minutes, until it's browned all over. Move it to a bowl. Add the remaining 1 tbsp vegetable oil and brown the rest of the chicken the same way.
Put all the chicken back in the pan. Whisk the sauce again so the cornstarch is mixed back in, and pour it over the chicken.

Cook, stirring, for 3 to 4 minutes, until the sauce bubbles and turns thick and glossy. You're cooking the chicken to 175°F, so if you have a thermometer, check the thickest piece. No thermometer? Cut one open: it's done when there's no pink left.
Turn off the heat and stir in 2 tbsp of the toasted sesame seeds.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch of salt.
Serve over the rice with the scallions and the last 1 tbsp of sesame seeds on top.
method_notes: All three coat bite size chicken in cornstarch, brown it in a skillet in batches and finish it in a soy based sauce thickened with cornstarch, with toasted sesame seeds and scallions on top. Spend With Pennies coats the chicken in egg, soy sauce and cornstarch and chills it for 15 minutes, then makes the sauce from chicken broth, brown sugar, soy sauce, sesame oil, ginger and garlic. Skinnytaste seasons the chicken with salt, pepper and a little starch and uses a sweetener, tomato paste and rice vinegar in the sauce, and Well Plated fries scallions, ginger and garlic first and sweetens with honey and rice vinegar. This follows Spend With Pennies scaled up by half for 1.5 lb of chicken, with thighs in place of breasts.
